about: Rkatsiteli is one of the oldest grape varieties in the world, native to the Republic of Georgia, and Dr. Konstantin Frank is the reason it grows in New York. Born in Odessa in 1899, Frank earned a doctorate in cold-climate viticulture and managed vineyards in Soviet Georgia before emigrating in 1951. In 1958 he bought land on the west shore of Keuka Lake, and while experimenting through the 1950s and 1960s he became the first to plant Rkatsiteli in the Finger Lakes. His family still runs the winery he founded in 1962.

The winery farms just under ten acres of Rkatsiteli on its Keuka Estate, on east-facing slopes between about 980 and 1,200 feet, with plantings from 1983, 1987 and 2003 in shallow, shale-rich silt loam. The 2024 is 77% Keuka fruit and 23% from a young plot on the Seneca Lake estate, planted in 2022; this is its first release. The grapes were destemmed and pressed directly, fermented cool in stainless steel without malolactic conversion, and kept entirely out of oak.

2024 was a warm, early year, with harvest running nearly two weeks ahead of normal and a long, settled autumn. The winemakers describe a strikingly aromatic white with tropical and herbal notes, passion fruit, pineapple and apricot over a grassy, pine-like edge, and a round, textured palate held up by lively acidity, finishing crisp. It is a lower-alcohol wine and a rare chance to taste a Georgian grape grown in New York.
facts: Direct pressed; stainless steel fermentation, no malolactic
